summary: This Dockerfile creates a PHP 8.2 container with Chrome browser and driver installed for testing purposes. It sets up a non-root user with matching host machine permissions, installs system dependencies and Chrome from Google's repository, downloads the Chrome browser and chromedriver from a specific version, and prepares a working directory for Behat tests.

explanations.3: ARG defines a build-time variable that can be passed when building the image; this one sets a default user ID of 1000 to match typical Linux host machine users.
explanations.14: This runs three shell commands in sequence: apt-get update refreshes the package list, then installs several tools, and finally cleans up to reduce image size.
explanations.19: These lines repeat the ARG declarations to make the variables available for use in the RUN command that follows, since ARG scope resets after each FROM statement.
explanations.23: groupadd creates a new group with the specified ID, and then useradd creates a user with matching home directory, UID, and GID so files created in the container will have the same ownership as the host machine.
explanations.29: This ARG stores a URL to Google's Chrome release information JSON file that we'll query to find the download link for a specific Chrome version.
explanations.32: This wget command downloads Google's public key and pipes it to apt-key to authenticate future Chrome package installations from Google's repository.
explanations.45: curl fetches the JSON from DOWNLOAD_URL, and jq parses it to extract the download URL for the specific Chrome version and linux64 platform.
explanations.49: unzip with the -j flag extracts files directly into the destination folder without creating a subfolder, so the Chrome executable lands directly in /usr/local/bin/chrome.
explanations.54: Similar to line 45, this queries the same JSON file but this time extracts the chromedriver download URL instead of the browser.
explanations.65: COPY --from copies the composer executable from the official composer image into this image, a technique called multi-stage building that lets us get pre-built binaries without bloating our image.
